author: CyberWire
articleText:
Anthropic disclosed that while reviewing its cybersecurity testing they discovered three cases where Claude AI escaped its sandbox environment and unintentionally hacked real-world organizations. These breaches occurred during "capture-the-flag" exercises. During the investigation, the company examined over 141,000 evaluations and found incidents dating back to April.
In these breaches, Anthropic noted that the models exploited weak passwords to gain access. Anthropic also acknowledged that human errors contributed to these incidents and said that future AI evaluations involving powerful autonomous systems will require stronger security controls.

articleTitle: EU launches new team to monitor AI compliance.
articleText:
The European Union (EU) has launched a new enforcement team that will be tasked with overseeing compliance with the region's AI Act. The compliance team will monitor for violations including AI-generated misinformation, explicit content, cyber treats, and other major risks. The act, which will come into enforcement Sunday, will be one of the most comprehensive efforts to regulate AI passed so far. Additionally, the EU has introduced whistleblower and compliance tools to support investigations. For companies found violating the AI Act, the EU can impose fines or restrict market access.
This enforcement initiative follows the EU's broader strategy to strengthen its oversight capabilities while simultaneously reducing dependence on US and Chinese technologies. Additionally, the EU is also increasing its investments in domestic AI capabilities to remain globally competative.

articleTitle: Health IT provider, CareCloud, suffers data breach.
articleText: CareCloud, a major health IT provider, has reported that in March 2026 the company suffered a data breach. The incident exposed at least 350,000 individuals and leaked personal, financial, and medical information. Stolen data includes Social Security numbers, financial information, and health records. In the breach, the attackers were able to compromise one of CareCloud's AWS environments from March 10 to March 16. The company has not identified the threat actor or how many people were impacted. Impacted individuals will be offered twenty-four months of identity protection and credit monitoring.
